effects: The signer sends exactly `assets` USDT to the vault (safeTransferFrom from msg.sender).
The vault mints sparkUSDTbc shares to `onBehalf`. The number comes from the current share price (previewDeposit), and no minimum applies.
The vault may move the deposited USDT into its liquidity adapter. This does not change what the signer pays or receives.
formats.shown: Deposit 1 USDT, with sparkUSDTbc shares sent to the onBehalf address. The number of shares minted is not shown.

findings.title: deposit does not show how many shares are minted; the contract sets the amount from the share price, with no minimum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol deposit: `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf);`. The calldata has no minShares parameter, so no field can show a bound.
findings.fix: None in the descriptor. The amount is read from storage at execution.

findings.title: deposit shows the share ticker as a separate raw constant field instead of placing it in the recipient line.
findings.evidence: descriptor deposit field {"label":"Share ticker","format":"raw","value":"$.metadata.constants.vaultTicker"}. The amount field label is 'Deposit asset' although it shows an amount.
findings.fix: Rename 'Deposit asset' to 'Amount'. Change the interpolatedIntent to 'Deposit {#.assets} for sparkUSDTbc shares to {#.onBehalf}' and drop the raw ticker field.

cases.notes: The signer sends 1 USDT, which the screen shows. The 1e18 shares go to 0xdead (signer null). The reader saw that shares go to 0xdead.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: The vault burns sparkUSDTbc shares from `onBehalf`. The number is previewWithdraw(assets), rounded up, and no maximum applies.
If msg.sender is not `onBehalf`, the vault spends that many shares from the signer's share allowance from `onBehalf`.
The receiver gets exactly `assets` USDT from the vault.
formats.shown: Withdraw exactly 16500 USDT to the receiver, with the Owner of the shares shown. The number of shares burned is not shown.

findings.title: withdraw does not show how many shares it burns; the amount comes from the share price, with no maximum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol withdraw: `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets); exit(...)`, then `deleteShares(onBehalf, shares)` in exit. Case 1: 16394.98 sparkUSDTbc out of the signer, not on screen.
findings.fix: None in the descriptor. The share amount is computed from storage and the calldata has no maxShares bound.

findings.title: withdraw interpolatedIntent does not say that the Owner's sparkUSDTbc shares are burned.
findings.evidence: interpolatedIntent 'Withdraw {#.assets} to {#.receiver}'. The Owner field exists, but the sentence does not name the shares as the source of the USDT.
findings.fix: Change the interpolatedIntent to 'Withdraw {#.assets} from sparkUSDTbc to {#.receiver}'.

cases.notes: The screen shows 16500 USDT in. The burn of 16394.98 sparkUSDTbc shares is not shown (it is computed). The reader guessed that shares leave but did not know the amount.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: The vault burns exactly `shares` sparkUSDTbc from `onBehalf`. If the signer is not onBehalf, the vault spends the signer's share allowance.
The receiver gets previewRedeem(shares) USDT. The share price sets this amount, and no minimum applies.
formats.shown: Redeem 6174.68 sparkUSDTbc to the receiver, with the Owner shown. Nothing states that USDT is received or how much.

findings.title: The redeem screen never names USDT as the asset paid out; only the share ticker hints at it.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol exit: `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets);` with asset = USDT (immutable 0xdac17f…). Descriptor redeem shows only shares, receiver and owner. Case 2: the signer receives 6213.199789 USDT, and the screen does not name USDT.
findings.fix: Change interpolatedIntent to 'Redeem {#.shares} for USDT to {#.receiver}'. Or add a field labelled 'Receive' whose value is $.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker.

findings.title: redeem does not show how much USDT is received; the amount comes from the share price, with no minimum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol redeem: `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares); exit(assets, shares, receiver, onBehalf);`. The calldata has no minAssets parameter.
findings.fix: None in the descriptor. The amount is read from storage at execution.

cases.notes: The screen shows the shares out. The USDT in (6213.199789) has no asset and no amount on screen. The reader guessed 'likely USDT' with no amount.

redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver,.worst: The redeem screen never names USDT as the asset paid out; only the share ticker hints at it.
